passages.title: Safety in the Workshop
passages.text: Every workshop has rules to keep workers safe. First, workers must wear goggles and gloves when they use power tools. Second, drinks and food are prohibited near the machines because a spill can cause accidents. Third, every workshop must have a fire extinguisher and a first aid box in an easy-to-reach place. If a worker gets a wound, he or she should clean it and report it to the supervisor immediately. These precautions help prevent injuries.

passages.title: Simple Machines
passages.text: Simple machines make work easier by changing the size or the direction of a force. A pulley helps people lift a heavy load by pulling a rope downward. A wedge, such as an axe, splits wood by turning a downward force into a sideways force. An inclined plane, for example a ramp, allows people to raise objects with less effort, but the distance becomes longer. These machines have been used for thousands of years, and they are still found inside modern machines.

passages.title: Units of Measurement
passages.text: Engineers around the world work with different measurement systems. Most countries use the metric system, with units such as kilograms, litres and metres. However, in the United States, imperial measurements such as pounds, gallons and inches are still common. This can cause confusion when engineers from different countries work together. A small error in conversion may be very costly. For this reason, engineers always check the units carefully before they start a project.

passages.title: Choosing the Right Material
passages.text: Engineers must choose materials carefully for every project. For a bridge, reinforced concrete is a good choice because it is strong and resists heavy loads. For windows, coated glass is often used, since the coating reduces heat from the sun. Stainless steel is popular in kitchens and hospitals because it does not rust and is easy to clean. Lumber is still common in house construction, but it needs protection from water. A wrong choice can make a building unsafe or too expensive.

passages.title: The Trebuchet
passages.text: The trebuchet is a type of siege engine from the Middle Ages. It was used to throw heavy stones over the walls of fortifications. A trebuchet has a long arm that turns around a pivot. At one end, there is a heavy counterweight, and at the other end, there is a sling with the projectile. When the counterweight falls, the arm moves and the sling throws the stone at high speed. It could throw a stone weighing over 100 kilograms. Later, gunpowder and cannons replaced these machines.

passages.title: Soft Skills for Engineers
passages.text: Engineers need more than technical knowledge. Employers also look for personal traits and skills. For example, curiosity helps engineers learn new things, and punctuality shows respect for other people's time. Good interpersonal skills are necessary because engineers work in teams. Some employers prefer a person with an outgoing personality, but this is not essential. Finally, competency in mathematics is important, since quantitative thinking is part of nearly every project.

passages.title: The Scientific Method
passages.text: Engineers and scientists often use a method to solve problems. First, they state a hypothesis, which is an idea that can be tested. Then, they plan the methodology and choose the variables. A control group does not receive the change, so the results can be compared. After the experiment, they collect data and infer a conclusion. If the results do not support the hypothesis, they change it and test again. This repeated procedure is called iteration.

passages.title: Heat and Energy
passages.text: When an engine runs, only part of its energy is used to move the car. The rest of the energy is lost as heat. This heat dissipates into the air, and it cannot be used again. For this reason, engineers try to reduce this loss by using better materials and designs. For example, a well-designed engine retains less heat in its parts. An engine with high efficiency uses less fuel and also produces less pollution.

passages.title: A Problem on the Production Line
passages.text: Last month, a car parts factory faced a serious problem. Many metal parts were coming off the production line with small cracks. The team first carried out problem identification and found that the machine was running too hot. They decided to attack the problem by changing the cooling system, which was the most cost-effective approach. After two tests, the number of damaged parts dropped from 12% to 2%. The manager deemed the result a success.

passages.title: From Idea to Product
passages.text: Many products start with an idea on a computer. First, the engineer prepares a technical drawing with CAD software. Next, the design is tested with computer simulations; for example, CFD shows how air moves around a car. After testing, the company makes a prototype and checks it for stresses and weak points. Finally, CAM software gives instructions to machines in the factory to produce the part. This process saves time and money because mistakes are found early.

passages.title: A Day at a Construction Site
passages.text: A civil engineer starts the day by walking around the site and checking the progress. Workers wear helmets and goggles, and the engineer checks that all precautions are in place. Then, the engineer meets the project manager to discuss the deadline and the materials that are needed. If a delivery is late, the engineer may need to push back the schedule. In the afternoon, the engineer reviews drawings and answers the workers' questions.

passages.title: The Crane
passages.text: A crane is a machine that lifts heavy loads and moves them from one place to another. A tower crane is used in tall building projects. It has a long arm and a counterweight at the opposite side, which keeps the crane balanced. The operator sits high in a small cabin and controls the load with levers. Because mass and distance affect the balance, a crane can lift only a limited weight. If a load is too heavy, the crane may fall.

passages.title: Why Engineers Need Soft Skills
passages.text: Technical skills are necessary for engineers, but they are not enough. Engineers must explain ideas to managers, clients and workers. Dependability is also important, because a team needs members who finish their tasks on time. Another useful trait is curiosity, which makes an engineer want to learn new methods. Finally, good judgment helps an engineer to make a reasonable decision when the situation is complicated. Companies want to employ people who have both technical and personal skills.

passages.title: The Catapult
passages.text: A catapult is a machine that throws an object, called a projectile, over a long distance. Early catapults used the energy stored in twisted ropes. When the ropes were released, the arm moved quickly and threw the object. Armies used catapults in warfare to attack fortifications and to throw stones, fire or even dead animals. Compared with a trebuchet, a catapult was smaller and easier to move, but it could not throw very heavy loads.

passages.title: Using a Multimeter
passages.text: A multimeter is a useful tool for measuring electricity in a circuit. With it, an engineer can measure voltage, current and resistance. Before taking a measurement, you should check the settings and choose the right range. If you set a low range for a high voltage, the device may be damaged. It is also important to remember not to touch the metal ends of the probes while measuring, because this can cause an electric shock. Always read the manual first.

passages.title: Why Do Metals Rust?
passages.text: Rust is a reddish-brown layer that forms on iron or steel when it comes into contact with water and oxygen. It makes the metal weak and can cause bridges, cars and pipes to break. Engineers use several methods to prevent rust. One method is to coat the metal with paint or another protective layer. Another is to use stainless steel, which contains chromium and does not rust easily. Regular inspection is also important because small spots of rust can be fixed before they become a serious problem.

passages.title: The Lever and Its Parts
passages.text: The lever is one of the oldest simple machines. It consists of a rigid bar, a fulcrum and a load. When someone pushes down on one end of the bar, the other end rises and lifts the load. The closer the fulcrum is to the load, the less effort is needed to lift it. This is called mechanical advantage. A wheelbarrow, scissors and a seesaw are all examples of levers. Without levers, many daily tasks would be much harder.

passages.title: Working with Imperial Units
passages.text: In the US, many engineers still work in imperial units. For example, they measure length in inches and feet, weight in pounds, and volume in gallons. This can be a problem when a project has international partners who use the metric system. In 1999, a space probe was lost because one team used pounds and another used kilograms. The error cost millions of dollars. Since then, many companies have required a careful conversion check to reduce the chance of such an error.

passages.title: Fire Safety
passages.text: Fire needs three things to burn: heat, fuel and oxygen. If one of them is removed, the fire stops. A small fire can be put out with a fire extinguisher, but you need to know how to use it. If the fire is too big, you should leave the building immediately and call the fire brigade. Never use water on an oil fire, because it can make the flames bigger. Companies should train their workers regularly and keep exits free of boxes and equipment.

passages.title: Building Roads and Bridges
passages.text: Roads and bridges are important parts of a country's infrastructure. Before building them, engineers carry out a topographical survey to study the shape of the land. After that, they prepare plans and choose materials such as concrete and reinforced steel. The project may be large-scale, like a highway, or small-scale, like a village road. Municipal governments often pay for local roads. Bridge engineers also consider factors such as traffic, weather and earthquakes. All these factors affect the cost and the design.

passages.title: Why Do Engineers Use Iteration?
passages.text: In engineering, the first design is rarely the best one. Engineers build a prototype, test it, find its weak points and then make improvements. This cycle is repeated many times and is called iteration. For example, the designers of a new phone may try ten different shapes before they find the best one. Although iteration takes time, it reduces inefficiency and gives a better final product. Customers often do not know about this hidden work.

passages.title: The Wheel and Axle
passages.text: The wheel and axle is a simple machine made of a large wheel fixed to a smaller rod, called an axle. When the wheel turns, the axle turns too. Because the wheel is larger, a small force on the wheel creates a bigger force on the axle. A steering wheel is a good example: the driver turns the large wheel easily, and the axle turns the car's tyres. Door knobs and screwdrivers also use this idea. Without the wheel and axle, many machines and vehicles would not exist.

passages.title: Safe Chemical Handling
passages.text: Chemicals are used in many laboratories and factories, but some of them can be dangerous. Before using any chemical, workers should read the label and learn about the risks. They should wear goggles, gloves and a lab coat. If a spill occurs, they must tell their supervisor, keep other people away and clean it up properly. Eating and drinking in the laboratory is prohibited. Chemicals should also be stored in a cool and dry place and kept away from flames.

passages.title: A Power Supply
passages.text: A power supply is a device that gives the right amount of electricity to the parts of a machine. The wall outlet gives alternating current, but most electronic devices use direct current with a lower voltage. The power supply changes the input voltage into the output voltage that the machine needs. If the output is too high, the components may be damaged. A good power supply also protects the device against sudden increases in the electricity. For this reason, engineers choose it carefully.

passages.title: Medieval Siege Warfare
passages.text: In the Middle Ages, castles were protected by thick stone walls, towers and fortifications. To capture a castle, armies used siege engines. A catapult threw stones over the walls, while a trebuchet was larger and stronger. Soldiers also used long ladders and rams to break the gates. Sometimes an army waited outside for months until the people inside ran out of food. Later, the invention of gunpowder and cannons changed siege warfare because walls could be destroyed from a distance.

passages.title: What Is a Job Interview Really About?
passages.text: In a job interview, the employer wants to know more than your degree and your competencies. Interviewers also ask questions to understand your traits, for example, whether you are dependable and punctual. They may ask you to solve a problem to see your judgment and quantitative thinking. It is a good idea to prepare examples from your past experience. Also, you should arrive early, dress properly and listen carefully to the questions. A calm and polite person is often preferred.

passages.title: Electric Circuits
passages.text: An electric circuit is a closed path in which electric current can flow. A simple circuit has a power source, such as a battery, wires and a component, such as a lamp. When the circuit is closed, the current flows and the lamp lights up. If there is a break in the wire, the current stops. Circuits may be series or parallel. In a series circuit, the same current passes through every component, while in a parallel circuit the current is divided. An integrated circuit is a tiny circuit on a chip.

passages.title: Why Do Engineers Use CAD?
passages.text: CAD stands for computer-aided design. Before CAD, engineers drew every plan by hand, and even a small change meant drawing everything again. Today, CAD software allows engineers to create precise two-dimensional and three-dimensional models on a computer. They can change dimensions quickly, rotate the model and test it. CAD files can be shared with colleagues around the world, which supports teamwork. Also, the same file can be used by CAM software to produce the part in a factory.

passages.title: Energy and the Work-Energy Principle
passages.text: Energy is the ability to do work. When a force moves an object over a distance, work is done and energy is transferred to the object. According to the work-energy principle, the work done on an object is equal to the change in its energy. For example, when a driver presses the brake, the brakes do work on the car. The car's energy decreases and it slows down. A faster car has more energy, so its stopping distance is longer. This is why speed limits are important near schools.

passages.title: Soft Skills in the Workplace
passages.text: Companies now pay more attention to soft skills when they hire engineers. A person with good interpersonal skills can work well in a team and talk to customers. Curiosity helps an engineer to find new solutions, while good judgment leads to wise decisions. Punctuality and dependability also show that the person respects colleagues. Some people think an outgoing person is better, but quiet people can also be very successful if they communicate clearly. A university degree shows knowledge, but traits show how a person works.
